Hi Louis,

I'd recommend checking that your Loc variable really contains
coordinates in metres, as assumed by the crs specifications you use,
and not kilometres as indicated by the variable names Xkm, Ykm.

Also remove the crs argument in inla.spde2.matern() as it does nothing.

Note that the new inla version uses the fmesher package for mesh
handling, which in most cases does exactly the same as old code, but
also handles sf objects etc more transparently, making coordinate
system handling a bit safer/correct.

For your specific error message, check the size of Loc, mesh$n,
spde1$n.spde, str(A1), as well as str(w1.NB.index), and
nrow(WISA_df_nNA), as the size discrepancy likely comes from one of
those being incorrect.

Finn

that size information is very useful;

I think you used something like length(Loc) instead of the intended
nrow(Loc), since the A1 matrix height is exactly half; 98244 vs 49122?

14083, as you noted, and this should be impossible for the current and
past 2D mesh code (for 1D "meshes" they can be different, but in a
well-defined way).
This means that we can ignore all follow-up errors; the inla.stack
error message simply detected this problem.
Are you absolutely sure you generated the spde1 object from this mesh,
and that there was no warning message or other thing?

If you just type

mesh

in the R console, what's the output?

Also,

str(fm_basis(mesh, loc = Loc))

Finn

parts:
Thanks,
I now see that even the mesh doesn't agree with itself about its own size;
You'll find that nrow(mesh$loc) and mesh$n are different although they
should be the same!!!

This is a strange bug as I don't see how it wasn't detected sooner; it
has to do with handling of "unused vertices" after the mesh
construction; these are removed, but it fails to update the "n"
element.

You can work around this in your code with
mesh$n <- nrow(mesh$loc)

Let me know if that solves your problem; I've updated fmesher so that
from 0.1.2.9002 it should no longer have this bug.

Finn

parts:
I just checked the old INLA code, and that code handled this
differently and shouldn't be affected by the same problem, so you can
temporarily revert to that by using
inla.setOption(fmesher.evolution=1L)
if needed.

Finn
